1	# WP-001: DOM Patch Functions
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Make the GUI project detail page fully dynamic by adding periodic polling for all project-related data (WP statuses, synthesis availability, project status, health badge) and fix the orchestrator runs section to update without flicker or scroll position loss by using targeted DOM patching instead of full innerHTML rebuilds.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Implement targeted DOM update functions that modify specific elements in-place when data changes, avoiding full page rebuilds and preserving interactive state (open modals, inline edits, scroll position).
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail.js` — new patch functions within the module
    14	
    15	## Deliverables
    16	
    17	- `_patchProjectStatus(newStatus)` — updates the status badge in the page header using `statusBadge(newStatus)` (which delegates to `UI.badge()`)
    18	- `_patchWpRow(wpId, newStatus, newPipelineTrack)` — updates a single WP row's status badge and pipeline track cells in-place; uses `statusBadge()` for status badges consistent with existing WP table rendering
    19	- `_patchSynthesisLink(visible)` — shows/hides the synthesis link row; injects the row if absent when `visible=true`, hides it when `visible=false`
    20	- `_patchHealthBadge(health)` — updates the health badge text and CSS class based on `work_packages_needing_reset` count
    21	- `_patchTimingInfo(timing)` — updates the timing display (duration, active time, pipeline runs) in-place
    22	
    23	## Dependencies
    24	
    25	- None
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. Each patch function performs compare-and-swap on text content and/or attributes — it does not replace the parent element or trigger a full subtree rebuild
    30	2. `_patchProjectStatus` uses `statusBadge()` / `UI.badge()` to render badge HTML, consistent with the initial render path
    31	3. `_patchWpRow` locates WP rows by data attribute or index and updates only the status badge and pipeline track cells, leaving the WP ID and assigned-to cells untouched
    32	4. `_patchSynthesisLink(true)` makes the synthesis link visible (injecting it if not present); `_patchSynthesisLink(false)` hides it
    33	5. All patch functions perform fresh DOM queries on each invocation — no cached element references are stored across poll cycles
    34	6. All new HTML rendered in patch functions uses `UI.badge()`, `UI.card()`, `UI.banner()`, or `statusBadge()` where applicable (zero raw `<span class="badge ...">` strings unless those helpers are insufficient)
    35	
    36	## Active Pipeline Stages
    37	
    38	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    39	
    40	## Estimated Complexity
    41	
    42	Medium
    43	
    44	## Rationale
    45	
    46	Targeted DOM patching (compare-and-swap on specific elements) preserves interactive state because the browser does not tear down and recreate DOM nodes. This avoids flicker, preserves focus/selection in inline editors, and eliminates the need to re-attach event listeners after each update cycle.
    47	
    48	## Rejected Approaches
    49	
    50	- **Full innerHTML rebuild every cycle** — this is the current project-list.js pattern, but the project detail page has richer interactive state (inline edits, modals, log preview widgets) that cannot survive a full DOM rebuild. Full rebuilds cause visible flicker from DOM teardown/recreation.
    51	- **Virtual DOM / morphdom library** — the GUI has a zero-dependency constraint; targeted updates on the known, stable DOM structure are simpler and sufficient.
    52	
    53	## Notes
    54	
    55	The WP rows must be identifiable by a stable selector (data attribute on `<tr>` keyed to `work_package_id`). The existing `renderProjectDetail` may need a minor adjustment to add `data-wp-id` attributes to table rows so `_patchWpRow` can locate them. The synthesis link row pattern (pre-rendered as hidden vs. injected on demand) should be decided during implementation — the plan suggests either approach. Patch functions should be no-ops when the target element is not found (defensive against race conditions during structural re-renders).
